typedef enum CaCompressionType {
        CA_COMPRESSION_XZ,
        CA_COMPRESSION_GZIP,
        CA_COMPRESSION_ZSTD,
        _CA_COMPRESSION_TYPE_MAX,
        _CA_COMPRESSION_TYPE_INVALID = -1,

        CA_COMPRESSION_DEFAULT =
#if HAVE_LIBZSTD
        CA_COMPRESSION_ZSTD,
#elif HAVE_LIBZ
        CA_COMPRESSION_GZIP,
#elif HAVE_LIBLZMA
        CA_COMPRESSION_XZ,
#else
        _CA_COMPRESSION_TYPE_INVALID
#endif
} CaCompressionType;
objects.description: Enumeration of supported compression backends, with a build-time-selected CA_COMPRESSION_DEFAULT. Values include XZ, GZIP, ZSTD, plus sentinels for max and invalid.

Opaque digest context object. Concrete structure is not defined in this header; it is managed via the provided API for creating, writing data, reading the resulting hash, resetting, and changing type.
Enumeration of supported digest algorithms for CaDigest. Provides SHA-256 and SHA-512/256, plus default, max, and invalid sentinels.
Binary identifier for a content-addressed chunk, storing a 32-byte digest (SHA-256 or SHA-512/256). Exposes byte-wise and 64-bit-word views.

functions.name: ca_compression_type_to_string
functions.description: Convert a CaCompressionType enum value to its human-readable name. Typical use is for logging or configuration serialization.
requirements: c should be a valid CaCompressionType value; behavior for _CA_COMPRESSION_TYPE_INVALID is unspecified.
The returned pointer refers to a constant string and must not be modified.

functions.name: ca_compression_type_from_string
functions.description: Parse a human-readable compression type name into a CaCompressionType enum value. Intended for reading configuration or user input.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string representing a known compression type.
Returns _CA_COMPRESSION_TYPE_INVALID for unrecognized input (exact semantics unspecified in header).

functions.name: ca_digest_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new digest context of the specified type (e.g., SHA256 or SHA512/256). On success stores the created context in *ret.
requirements: ret must be non-NULL and point to a location where the created CaDigest* will be stored.
t must be a valid CaDigestType (not _CA_DIGEST_TYPE_INVALID).
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned context with ca_digest_free.

functions.name: ca_digest_free
functions.description: Free a CaDigest context and return NULL for convenience. Intended to be used for cleanup (and with the provided ca_digest_freep helper).
requirements: d must be a CaDigest* previously obtained from ca_digest_new or ca_digest_ensure_allocated.
Do not use the context after freeing it.
The function returns NULL (per common pattern); assign the return value back to your variable if you rely on NULLing.

functions.name: ca_digest_ensure_allocated
functions.description: Ensure that *d holds a valid CaDigest of the given type, allocating it if *d is NULL. If already allocated, the function may leave it as-is or adjust it as needed.
requirements: d must be non-NULL.
t must be a valid CaDigestType (not _CA_DIGEST_TYPE_INVALID).
On success, *d will reference an initialized digest context that the caller must later free with ca_digest_free.

functions.name: ca_digest_write
functions.signature: void ca_digest_write(CaDigest *d, const void *p, size_t l);
functions.description: Update the digest with l bytes from buffer p. Use for streaming data into the digest.
requirements: d must be a valid, initialized CaDigest*.
If l > 0, p must be a valid pointer to at least l bytes; p may be NULL only when l == 0.
Must be called before finalizing/reading if you want the data to affect the digest.

functions.name: ca_digest_read
functions.description: Return a pointer to the current digest value (raw bytes). Use ca_digest_get_size to determine the length.
requirements: d must be a valid, initialized CaDigest*.
The returned memory must not be modified by the caller.
Size of the digest can be obtained via ca_digest_get_size(d).
Lifetime/validity of the returned pointer is not specified in the header; if in doubt, copy the bytes immediately.

functions.name: ca_digest_reset
functions.description: Reset the digest context to its initial state, discarding any previously written data.
requirements: d must be a valid CaDigest*.
After reset, previous digest_read results become stale; recompute as needed.

functions.name: ca_digest_get_size
functions.description: Return the digest output size in bytes for the context’s current type.
requirements: d must be a valid CaDigest*.
Returned size corresponds to the current type; changing type may change this value.

functions.name: ca_digest_get_type
functions.description: Return the digest algorithm type currently configured for the context.
requirements: d must be a valid CaDigest*.

functions.name: ca_digest_get_name
functions.description: Return a human-readable name for the digest context’s current type.
requirements: d must be a valid CaDigest*.
The returned pointer refers to a constant string and must not be modified.

functions.name: ca_digest_type_size
functions.description: Return the output size in bytes for the specified digest type.
requirements: t should be a valid CaDigestType (behavior for _CA_DIGEST_TYPE_INVALID is unspecified).

functions.name: ca_digest_type_to_string
functions.description: Convert a CaDigestType enum value to its human-readable name.
requirements: t should be a valid CaDigestType; behavior for invalid values is unspecified.
The returned pointer refers to a constant string and must not be modified.

functions.name: ca_digest_type_from_string
functions.description: Parse a human-readable digest type name into a CaDigestType enum value.
requirements: name must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string representing a known digest type.
Returns _CA_DIGEST_TYPE_INVALID for unrecognized input (exact behavior unspecified in header).

functions.name: ca_digest_set_type
functions.description: Change the digest algorithm used by the context to the specified type.
requirements: d must be a valid CaDigest*.
t must be a valid CaDigestType (not _CA_DIGEST_TYPE_INVALID).
Changing type may invalidate previously computed results; caller should assume the context is effectively reset (not explicitly documented).

functions.name: ca_chunk_id_parse
functions.description: Parse a textual chunk ID into a 32-byte CaChunkID structure. The textual form is the hexadecimal representation of the ID.
requirements: v must be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string containing a 64-character hexadecimal representation (no separators) of a 32-byte ID.
ret must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for a CaChunkID.
On success, returns ret; on failure, behavior is unspecified in header.

functions.name: ca_chunk_id_format
functions.description: Format a 32-byte CaChunkID as a 64-character hexadecimal string plus terminating NUL into the provided buffer and return v.
requirements: id must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid CaChunkID.
v must point to a writable buffer of at least CA_CHUNK_ID_FORMAT_MAX bytes (64 hex chars + 1 NUL).
The returned pointer is v; buffer contents are owned by the caller.

functions.name: ca_chunk_id_make
functions.signature: int ca_chunk_id_make(CaDigest *digest, const void *p, size_t l, CaChunkID *ret);
functions.description: Compute a CaChunkID for the given data using the provided digest context and store it in ret. The chunk ID is a 32-byte digest (e.g., SHA256 or SHA512/256).
requirements: digest must be a valid, initialized CaDigest* whose digest output size is exactly CA_CHUNK_ID_SIZE (32 bytes).
ret must be non-NULL and point to writable storage for a CaChunkID.
If l > 0, p must point to at least l bytes; p may be NULL only when l == 0.

functions.name: ca_chunk_id_format_path
functions.signature: char* ca_chunk_id_format_path(const char *prefix, const CaChunkID *chunkid, const char *suffix, char buffer[]);
functions.description: Construct a filesystem path string from an optional prefix, a formatted chunk ID, and an optional suffix, writing the result into buffer and returning buffer.
requirements: chunkid must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid CaChunkID.
buffer must be large enough to hold the full result; use CA_CHUNK_ID_PATH_SIZE(prefix, suffix) to size it.
prefix may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string.
suffix may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string.
The returned pointer is buffer; buffer contents are owned by the caller.

data_types.description: A NUL-terminated text string with no required structure or character set constraints beyond being valid C-string data. May contain any bytes except the terminating NUL; used for free-form names, prefixes, or suffixes.

A byte buffer of any length (including zero) whose contents are treated as opaque binary data. No encoding or structure is required; used directly as input to functions like hashing or processing raw bytes.
A textual representation consisting solely of hexadecimal digits (0-9, a-f or A-F). In this context, typically a fixed-length 64-character lowercase hex string representing 32 bytes of binary data.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs for generic C strings used by:
# - ca_compression_type_from_string (expects names like "xz", "gzip", "zstd" or arbitrary)
# - ca_digest_type_from_string (expects names like "sha256", "sha512_256" or arbitrary)
# - ca_chunk_id_format_path (expects prefix/suffix strings; any NUL-terminated C-strings)
#
# The fuzzer framework will draw strings from the provided byte buffer. We therefore
# pack multiple interesting, NUL-terminated strings back-to-back in the buffer. The
# stubs may request several FUZZ_PARAM_STR values; this buffer should contain a mix of:
# - Valid compression names: "xz", "gzip", "zstd"
# - Valid digest names: "sha256", "sha512_256"
# - Edge-case strings for prefixes/suffixes: empty, very short, long (<=64), with slashes,
#   dots, spaces, unicode-like UTF-8, and characters often used in paths.
# - Random additional strings to add variation while remaining valid C-strings.
#
# Constraints:
# - Total size <= 4096 bytes
# - Strings are valid C-strings (no embedded NUL; we terminate with NUL explicitly)
# - Deterministic with the provided seed, but still varied.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

VALID_COMPRESSION = ["xz", "gzip", "zstd"]
VALID_DIGEST = ["sha256", "sha512_256"]

# Path-ish interesting tokens for prefix/suffix construction
INTERESTING_PATHS = [
    "",  # empty allowed
    "/",  # root
    ".",
    "..",
    "tmp",
    "var/lib/ca",
    "prefix",
    "suffix",
    "leading/slash/",
    "trailing",
    "multi/level/path",
    "with spaces",
    "dots...and...more",
    "special-_.~!$&'()@",
    "unicode-π-中文-😊",  # UTF-8 payload
]

# Additional arbitrary names for invalid-path testing of from_string parsers
ARBITRARY_NAMES = [
    "",  # empty
    "none",
    "unknown",
    "sha",
    "sha-256",
    "sha512/256",
    "SHA256",  # case sensitivity
    "ZSTD",     # case sensitivity
    "gz",
    "xz2",
    "lzo",
    "brotli",
    "123",
    "a" * 63,
]

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./ "

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))

def _cap64(s: str) -> str:
    # ca_chunk_id_format_path test clamps to 64; we keep within 64
    if len(s.encode('utf-8')) <= 64:
        return s
    # Truncate on code-point boundary by iteratively shortening bytes
    b = s.encode('utf-8')[:64]
    # ensure valid utf-8; if not, back off
    while True:
        try:
            return b.decode('utf-8', errors='strict')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            b = b[:-1]
            if not b:
                return ""

def _emit_cstr(buf: bytearray, s: str) -> None:
    # Ensure no embedded NULs; replace with space
    if "\x00" in s:
        s = s.replace("\x00", " ")
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    # Ensure buffer size constraint; leave room for NUL
    if len(buf) + len(b) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL:
        return
    buf += b
    buf.append(0)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    buf = bytearray()

    # 1) Ensure at least one valid compression and digest names appear early
    for name in rng.sample(VALID_COMPRESSION, k=len(VALID_COMPRESSION)):
        _emit_cstr(buf, name)
    for name in rng.sample(VALID_DIGEST, k=len(VALID_DIGEST)):
        _emit_cstr(buf, name)

    # 2) Include empty string once (valid C-string for prefixes/suffixes)
    _emit_cstr(buf, "")

    # 3) Add a mixture of path-like prefixes and suffixes (capped to 64)
    chosen_paths = rng.sample(INTERESTING_PATHS, k=min(len(INTERESTING_PATHS), 8))
    for p in chosen_paths:
        _emit_cstr(buf, _cap64(p))

    # 4) Add some arbitrary names (potentially invalid for parsers)
    for nm in rng.sample(ARBITRARY_NAMES, k=min(len(ARBITRARY_NAMES), 8)):
        _emit_cstr(buf, _cap64(nm))

    # 5) Add randomized valid-looking prefixes/suffixes of various lengths up to 64
    for _ in range(8):
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 64)
        _emit_cstr(buf, s)

    # 6) Add additional valid identifiers with separators, to exercise path joining
    for _ in range(6):
        parts = [
            _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8),
            _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 6),
            _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 10),
        ]
        s = "/".join(filter(None, parts))
        _emit_cstr(buf, _cap64(s))

    # 7) Intersperse repeats of valid canonical names to increase their presence
    for _ in range(3):
        _emit_cstr(buf, rng.choice(VALID_COMPRESSION))
        _emit_cstr(buf, rng.choice(VALID_DIGEST))

    # Final safety: ensure non-empty output
    if not buf:
        _emit_cstr(buf, "xz")

    return bytes(buf)

import random
import os
import struct

# This generator targets inputs for FUZZ_PARAM_STR used to build a 64-char lowercase
# hexadecimal string for ca_chunk_id_parse. The fuzzer stub converts the provided
# bytes into hex nybbles deterministically, cycling over the buffer if shorter than 32.
# Therefore, any non-empty byte buffer is acceptable; to exercise different code paths
# and produce diverse chunk IDs, we generate variable-length data with patterns and
# randomness while ensuring size <= 1024 (the stub truncates beyond that anyway).

MAX_SIZE = 1024

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix structured patterns and randomness to cover varied byte distributions.
    parts = []

    # 1) Pure random chunk
    m = rng.randint(0, n)
    parts.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(m)))

    # 2) Repeating single-byte pattern
    if m < n and rng.random() < 0.9:
        v = rng.randrange(256)
        k = rng.randint(0, n - m)
        parts.append(bytes([v]) * k)
        m += k

    # 3) Incrementing sequence
    if m < n and rng.random() < 0.8:
        k = rng.randint(0, n - m)
        start = rng.randrange(256)
        seq = bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF) for i in range(k))
        parts.append(seq)
        m += k

    # 4) Boundary/interesting byte values sprinkled in
    interesting = [0x00, 0x01, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFE, 0xFF]
    if m < n and rng.random() < 0.8:
        k = min(len(interesting), n - m)
        sample = rng.sample(interesting, k)
        parts.append(bytes(sample))
        m += k

    # 5) Fill remaining with random if needed
    if m < n:
        parts.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n - m)))

    return b"".join(parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a size between 1 and 1024 inclusive (stub requires at least 1 byte; it truncates >1024).
    # Bias towards sizes around 1, 16, 32, 64, 256, 1024 to influence cycling behavior and full coverage.
    choices = [1, 2, 4, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 33, 48, 64, 128, 256, 512, 768, 1024]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        size = rng.choice(choices)
    else:
        size = rng.randint(1, MAX_SIZE)

    # Compose bytes with mixed structure.
    data = _rand_bytes(rng, size)

    # Ensure non-empty and within limit (already guaranteed by construction).
    if not data:
        data = b"\x00"
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]

    return data
